messages.subject: Re: getting started in June 2013 page not found error RStudio hosted server
parts:
Hi Kevin, there's no ~/ShinyApps directory in your account. (You're sure you created that directory on the RStudio server, not on your local machine?)


On Tue, Jun 4, 2013 at 7:55 PM, Kevin Little <kli...@iecodesign.com> wrote:
I'm grateful to the developers of shiny and impressed by all the examples and questions on the google group discussion.

Despite reading earlier posts and the tutorial, I am stuck using the Rstudio server to run the googleVis example.

On the RStudio-hosted Shiny Server, I have the googleVis example server.R and ui.R files stored in ~ShinyApps/myApp1 directory.

Earlier neophytes have stumbled at this point and I know I have to point my browser to the right location, not use runApp() function in the server RStudio console.

The set up email next tells me the location is supposed to be http://spark.rstudio.com/iecodesign/myApp1/

when I point to that URL, I get Page Not found error. 

I read the April 8 post from Stephane Laurent solved by Winston Chang (wrong directory path issue) but I don't see my solution.

Thank you in advance for help , I hope to have more interesting questions and examples soon.

--

messages.subject: Re: getting started in June 2013 page not found error RStudio hosted server
parts:
It looks like you have a directory named '~' in your home directory, and ShinyApps is a subdirectory of that.

In Unix-land, the ~ character actually refers to your home directory, not a directory named '~', so you need to move ShinyApps to your home directory. Then you can also remove the '~' directory.

-Winston
